keyVerseText: Is not the whole land before thee? separate thyself, I pray thee, from me: if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if thou depart to the right hand, then I will go to the left.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun שְׂמֹאול (sᵉmôʼwl) derives from a primitive root possibly related to שִׂמְלָה (simlâh), meaning a garment or covering. This etymology suggests a conceptual link between the idea of wrapping or enveloping and the direction 'left,' which in ancient Hebrew thought also connotes the north side, often seen as the dark or shaded side. Thus, the root sense enriches the common English gloss by implying not just a spatial direction but a sense of orientation related to covering or enclosure.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, שְׂמֹאול consistently refers to the left side or left hand, occurring 53 times with varied translations such as 'or to the left,' 'on the left,' and 'in his left hand.' The term also denotes the north side when facing east, highlighting an orientation system rooted in ancient Near Eastern culture. This consistency in usage reveals the word's fundamental role in describing spatial relationships and directions in biblical narratives.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שְׂמֹאול as 'left' or 'north' enriches our grasp of biblical symbolism and divine ordering. The left side, often contrasted with the right (יָמִין), can imply human weakness or lesser honor, while the right hand symbolizes strength and blessing. Recognizing this linguistic and cultural nuance helps believers appreciate biblical texts' depth, where physical orientation reflects spiritual realities. Moreover, the concept of 'covering' embedded in the root reminds us of God's protective presence enveloping His people, even on the 'left' or less honored side.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 13:9 presents a choice between the left and right hand, stating, 'if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if thou depart to the right hand, then I will go to the left.' Here, שְׂמֹאול underscores the act of separation and peaceful division of land between Abram and Lot. The word's meaning as 'left' or 'north' enriches the verse by highlighting the deliberate orientation and mutual respect in their decision, illustrating trust in God's provision regardless of physical position.
